learn_synthetic_check.name: synthetic_check
learn_synthetic_check.title: Learning run: synthetic_check
learn_synthetic_check.note: Synthetic data: procedural faces with scripted movements and invented labels, laid out like CASME II. This run checks that the folds, models, calibration and controls are wired correctly. It is not a benchmark and says nothing about human micro-expressions.
rows: random guess with the training frequencies
logistic regression: pattern + timing + AU evidence

prior.label: random guess with the training frequencies

linear.label: logistic regression: pattern + timing + AU evidence

shuffled_labels.name: shuffled_labels
shuffled_labels.reading: training labels were permuted; the held-out score should sit at chance (0.19). It is 0.18 - as expected.

identity_probe.name: identity_probe
identity_probe.reading: subject identity is decoded from the features at 40% against 8% by chance (12 subjects): the features carry identity, so a clip-level split would partly reward recognising faces. The folds here are subject-disjoint, which is what keeps this from inflating the reported numbers

leakage_gap.name: leakage_gap
leakage_gap.reading: with clip-level folds the same model scores UF1 0.69 against 0.73 with subject-disjoint folds (difference -0.04): no flattering showed up here, which on a small or synthetic set can be noise and does not make a clip-level split safe. Only the subject-disjoint number says anything about new people.

latency.note: feature extraction = landmarks + stabilisation + dense flow + AU engine on the clip; it dominates model inference

learn_synthetic_check.caveat: Numbers are subject-independent and pooled over folds; intervals resample subjects. They describe this dataset, this label scheme and these annotations - not people in general, and not deception or emotion detection.

summary.corpus: 240 phantom clips, 372 scripted movements, 42 movement-free clips; 6 face identities (A-C calibration, D-F test)
summary.note: synthetic phantoms: instrument calibration, not accuracy on human faces

spotting.rule: the threshold with the best spotting F1 on the calibration split among those within the false-alarm budget

sensitivity.x_axis: true size of the movement: its largest regional displacement, as % of the distance between the eyes

scope.fitted_on_calibration_faces: engine settings (eta, temper, size prior), spotting threshold, amplitude-interval widening, category conformal thresholds
scope.fitted_on_all_faces: the two smallest-detectable-movement factors (sensitivity.mda_check), because they only rescale a reported quantity; checked by refitting on each identity group (sensitivity.mda_split)
scope.held_out_test_faces: summary.*_test, spotting.table[*].test, engine.test, engine.amplitude_interval (coverage), categories.*.coverage_test, controls
scope.all_faces_descriptive: spotting.by_camera, spotting.by_nuisance, spotting.movement_free, sensitivity.envelope, sensitivity.grades, sensitivity.fidelity, engine.by_snr, engine.by_camera: these describe the corpus as a whole and were not used to fit anything

phantom_eval.caveat: Synthetic phantoms with scripted movements. These numbers calibrate and characterise the instrument; they say nothing about accuracy on human faces.
